messages:
alex: quick heads-up — our latest mix-quant candidate (fp8 + int4 fallback) shows a small perf win but a clear quality delta on structured outputs. seeing JSON fields reordered and occasional extra tokens in nested lists.

priya: can you paste the failing eval example?

alex: repro snippet from eval run 2026-03-17 21:12 UTC:
```
input: '{\"items\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"apple\"},{\"id\":2,\"name\":\"pear\"}]}'
expected: '{\"items\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"apple\"},{\"id\":2,\"name\":\"pear\"}]}'
actual: '{\"items\":[{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"apple\"},{\"name\":\"pear\",\"id\":2}]}'
note: keys reordered + occasional trailing \\\u201c,\\u201d after arrays in some cases
```

jamal: that looks like a floating point nondeterminism -> formatter ordering issue. Could be kernel ordering change during kv-merge or small probability reordering when parallel reduction triggers different associative ops.

wei: profiling dump attached (short):
```
# profile excerpt
model: raptor-3b-mix
seq_len: 1024
kernel selection path: aten->fused_matmul->fp8_vec4 (fast path) when batch_size<=8
fallback kernel: int4_dequant (used on tail iterations when cache misaligns)
p95 latency: baseline fp32 138ms -> mix-quant 125ms
tokens/s: baseline 1650 -> 1840
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.912 -> 0.873
batching heuristic: dynamic-aggressive -> caused more fragmented batches (avg batch 5.6 -> 3.9)
```

priya: kv_cache_hit_ratio drop is suspicious. Are we evicting prefixes incorrectly after calibration?

alex: good call — I saw extra cache invalidations in the trace. deploy-bot shows a routing change around the same time (canary rollout of new kernel selector).

deploy-bot: canary rollout 2026-03-17T20:58Z: kernel-selector v2 deployed to 10% traffic in us-west1.

wei: code path note: v2 selector uses a cheaper heuristic that favors fp8_vec4 for sequences < 512 and will switch kernels mid-sequence if kv segments misalign. That mid-sequence switch can reorder internal accum reductions on some fused kernels.

sara: QA ran regression evals (run id qa-331) — aggregated metrics:
- structured-accuracy drop: 3.9% absolute on JSON schema tests
- hallucination rate: +2.6% (examples where model invents extra list members)
- token-error anomalies concentrated on nested arrays

jamal: hypothesis: combination of mid-sequence kernel switch + reduced batch sizes changes floating point summation order -> tiny numeric diffs -> formatter heuristics sometimes flip key order when scoring/serializing objects. Also calibration for int4 fallback might be using per-tensor scale that underflows for small dynamic ranges.

priya: action items:
1) alex -> roll selector back from v2 canary (stop 10% rollout) and redeploy v1 routing in us-west1. (priority: high)
2) wei -> add guard to avoid mid-sequence kernel switches unless KV segments align exactly; instrument counters. (priority: high)
3) jamal -> run deterministic numeric regression with fixed kernel ordering (seed, single-thread) across 1000 evals to confirm non-determinism source. (priority: medium)
4) sara/qa-bot -> run focused structured-output evals with both calibration profiles (old/new) and attach diffs. (priority: high)
5) priya -> verify calibration config used for int4 fallback; ensure per-channel calibration for small-range tensors. (priority: medium)

qa-bot: scheduled qa-331-delta job: https://ci.redwood/suites/qa-331-delta (results pending)

alex: reproduction steps I used:
- checkout: serve-runtime@mixquant/2026-03-16
- model: raptor-3b-mix (pinned commit)
- start server: ./serve --kernel-selector=v2 --batch-heuristic=dynamic-aggressive --calib=int4-default
- run: scripts/eval_structured.sh --cases nested-arrays --seed 42 --runs 50
- artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/qa/qa-331/artifacts/1972104322-try1

wei: quick mitigation: force kernel-selector to prefer stable-kernel ordering flag --stable-kernel-order until we patch selector heuristics. Should be cheap.

priya: agreed. alex, can you flip the flag in canary now?

alex: flipping flag in canary -> updating config...

deploy-bot: config update: kernel-selector.stable_kernel_order=true applied to canary cluster us-west1 at 2026-03-17T21:05Z

jamal: while mitigated, we still need root cause. I'll start the numeric determinism runs and a small tool to diff JSON normalization after generation (to separate serialization noise from true token-level hallucination).

sara: QA will prioritize the nested-array suite and also run with batch-heuristic=conservative to see if batching fragmentation correlated.

alex: thanks team. I'll document the triage in the incident board and link the eval diffs. If anyone finds a quick reproducible seed where keys reorder deterministically, paste it here so we can bisect kernel change. :pray:
